<style>
@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Playfair+Display:ital,wght@0,400;0,600;0,700;1,400&family=Alice&family=Montserrat:wght@300;400;500;600;700;800&family=Lora:ital,wght@0,400;0,500;0,600;0,700;1,400&display=swap');

:root {
  --color-primary:        #1380da;
  --color-primary-light:  #64b7f0;
  --color-primary-pale:   #d0e9fd;
  --color-primary-bright: #2e8eff;
  --color-accent-blue:    #031aec;
  --color-accent-indigo:  #0b108b;
  --color-navy:           #07276e;
  --color-navy-deep:      #03325e;
  --color-white:          #ffffff;
  --color-gray:           #666666;
  --color-gray-blue:      #83b1d1;
  --color-gray-light:     #d4e1ed;
  --font-heading:    'Playfair Display', Georgia, serif;
  --font-body:       'Lora', Georgia, serif;
  --font-ui:         'Montserrat', sans-serif;
  --max-width:       1200px;
  --border-radius:   6px;
  --shadow-sm:  0 1px 3px rgba(3,50,94,0.08);
  --shadow-md:  0 4px 12px rgba(3,50,94,0.12);
  --shadow-lg:  0 8px 30px rgba(3,50,94,0.16);
}

/* ── PROCESS CARDS CAROUSEL ── */
.process-track-wrapper {
  position: relative;
  width: 100%;
  overflow: hidden;
}

.process-track-wrapper::before,
.process-track-wrapper::after {
  content: '';
  position: absolute;
  top: 0; bottom: 0;
  width: 60px;
  z-index: 2;
  pointer-events: none;
}

.process-track-wrapper::before {
  left: 0;
  background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--color-white), transparent);
}

.process-track-wrapper::after {
  right: 0;
  background: linear-gradient(270deg, var(--color-white), transparent);
}

.process-track {
  display: flex;
  gap: 24px;
  padding: 10px 40px 20px;
  overflow-x: auto;
  scroll-snap-type: x mandatory;
  -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch;
  scrollbar-width: thin;
  scrollbar-color: var(--color-primary-pale) transparent;
}

.process-track::-webkit-scrollbar {
  height: 6px;
}

.process-track::-webkit-scrollbar-track {
  background: transparent;
}

.process-track::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb {
  background: var(--color-primary-pale);
  border-radius: 3px;
}

.process-card {
  flex: 0 0 280px;
  scroll-snap-align: start;
  background: #f8fafc;
  border: 1px solid var(--color-gray-light);
  border-radius: var(--border-radius);
  padding: 28px 24px;
  transition: box-shadow 0.3s ease, transform 0.3s ease;
}

.process-card:hover {
  box-shadow: var(--shadow-md);
  transform: translateY(-3px);
}

.process-card .step-num {
  display: inline-block;
  width: 32px; height: 32px;
  line-height: 32px;
  text-align: center;
  background: var(--color-primary);
  color: #fff;
  border-radius: 50%;
  font-family: var(--font-ui);
  font-size: 0.8rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  margin-bottom: 14px;
}

.process-card h4 {
  font-family: var(--font-ui);
  font-size: 0.95rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  color: var(--color-navy-deep);
  margin-bottom: 10px;
  line-height: 1.3;
}

.process-card p {
  font-family: var(--font-body);
  font-size: 0.85rem;
  color: var(--color-gray);
  line-height: 1.65;
}

.process-dots {
  display: flex;
  justify-content: center;
  gap: 8px;
  margin-top: 20px;
}

.process-dots span {
  width: 8px; height: 8px;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: var(--color-gray-light);
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: background 0.3s;
}

.process-dots span.active {
  background: var(--color-primary);
}

/* ── COMPARISON TABLE ── */
.uv-compare-table {
  width: 100%;
  border-collapse: collapse;
  font-family: var(--font-body);
  font-size: 0.9rem;
}

.uv-compare-table thead th {
  font-family: var(--font-ui);
  font-size: 0.78rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  letter-spacing: 1px;
  color: var(--color-navy-deep);
  background: var(--color-primary-pale);
  padding: 14px 18px;
  text-align: left;
  border-bottom: 2px solid var(--color-primary);
}

.uv-compare-table tbody td {
  padding: 14px 18px;
  color: var(--color-gray);
  line-height: 1.6;
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-gray-light);
}

.uv-compare-table tbody td:first-child {
  font-family: var(--font-ui);
  font-weight: 600;
  color: var(--color-navy-deep);
  white-space: nowrap;
}

.uv-compare-table tbody tr:last-child td {
  border-bottom: none;
}

.uv-compare-table tbody tr:hover {
  background: #f8fafc;
}

/* ── BENEFITS GRID ── */
.tf-benefit-item {
  display: flex;
  align-items: flex-start;
  gap: 14px;
  padding: 10px 0;
}

.tf-benefit-dot {
  flex-shrink: 0;
  width: 8px;
  height: 8px;
  background: var(--color-primary);
  border-radius: 50%;
  margin-top: 7px;
}

.tf-benefit-item p {
  font-family: var(--font-body);
  font-size: 0.92rem;
  color: var(--color-gray);
  line-height: 1.7;
}

.tf-benefit-item strong {
  color: var(--color-navy-deep);
}

/* ── FAQ STYLES ── */
.faq-item {
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-gray-light);
  padding: 24px 0;
}

.faq-item:last-child {
  border-bottom: none;
}

.faq-q {
  font-family: var(--font-ui);
  font-size: 1rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  color: var(--color-navy-deep);
  cursor: pointer;
  display: flex;
  justify-content: space-between;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 16px;
}

.faq-q::after {
  content: '+';
  font-size: 1.3rem;
  font-weight: 300;
  color: var(--color-primary);
  transition: transform 0.3s;
  flex-shrink: 0;
}

.faq-item.open .faq-q::after {
  content: '\2212';
}

.faq-a {
  max-height: 0;
  overflow: hidden;
  transition: max-height 0.4s ease, padding 0.3s ease;
  padding-top: 0;
}

.faq-item.open .faq-a {
  max-height: 600px;
  padding-top: 14px;
}

.faq-a p {
  font-family: var(--font-body);
  font-size: 0.92rem;
  color: var(--color-gray);
  line-height: 1.75;
}

/* ── SCROLL ANIMATIONS ── */
.cap-page-fade {
  opacity: 0;
  transform: translateY(20px);
  transition: opacity 0.6s ease, transform 0.6s ease;
}

.cap-page-fade.visible {
  opacity: 1;
  transform: translateY(0);
}

/* ── RESPONSIVE ── */
@media (max-width: 900px) {
  .process-card { flex: 0 0 260px; }
  .uv-compare-table { font-size: 0.82rem; }
  .uv-compare-table thead th,
  .uv-compare-table tbody td { padding: 10px 12px; }
}

@media (max-width: 600px) {
  .process-card { flex: 0 0 240px; }
}
</style>

settings.editor:
UV flatbed printing is a digital printing process in which specially formulated UV-reactive inks are applied directly onto the surface of a material using an inkjet print head. As the ink is deposited, it is immediately exposed to ultraviolet light, which cures — or polymerizes — the ink almost instantly, bonding it firmly to the substrate.

Unlike conventional printing methods that rely on heat drying or solvent evaporation, UV curing is near-instantaneous and requires no drying time. This means faster production, less risk of smearing, and a finished surface that is immediately ready for use.

Because the printer operates on a flat, open bed rather than feeding material through rollers, it can accommodate a wide range of rigid and semi-rigid substrates at varying thicknesses — including plastic sheet, wood, metal, glass, foam board, and more. This direct-to-substrate capability makes it one of the most versatile printing methods available for both commercial and industrial applications.

settings.title: Our UV Flatbed Printing Machine & Capabilities

settings.editor:
Our UV flatbed printer is configured for commercial and industrial production, handling a broad range of materials and project sizes with consistent, high-quality output.

Key capabilities include:

  • High-resolution output — accurate color reproduction and crisp fine detail
  • Direct printing on thick materials — prints on materials up to several inches thick with no surface pre-treatment required for most substrates
  • Wide material compatibility — acrylic, polycarbonate, PVC, aluminum, wood, glass, foam board, and more
  • UV-cured ink durability — scratch-resistant, fade-resistant, and durable for both indoor and outdoor applications
  • White ink capability — for printing on dark, transparent, or colored substrates
  • Scalable for any project size — from single custom pieces to large production runs
UV flatbed printing is used across a wide range of industries and project types wherever high-quality, durable printing on rigid surfaces is needed. Common applications include:

• Custom signs and retail displays — vibrant, professional signage printed directly onto acrylic, PVC, aluminum, or foam board
  • Decorative wall panels and architectural graphics — large-format imagery and patterns on rigid panel materials for interior and commercial spaces
  • Branded products and personalized gifts — logos, artwork, and custom text printed directly onto finished items
  • Industrial labeling and equipment tags — permanent, durable identification marks on plastic or metal components that won’t peel or fade
  • Artwork and photo reproductions — gallery-quality reproductions printed directly onto acrylic, wood, or metal
  • Packaging prototypes and product mockups — accurate visual representations of finished packaging for review and approval
Have a project in mind? Our team can help you determine whether UV flatbed printing is the right process for your material, design, and volume requirements. Contact Us
Understanding where UV flatbed printing fits relative to other methods helps you make the right call for your project.

1

File Submission

Submit your design file for review. We accept vector formats and high-resolution raster files, and our team can advise on artwork preparation to ensure the best possible output quality for your chosen material.

2

Material Selection

Choose the substrate you want us to print on — or bring your own. We work with acrylic, polycarbonate, PVC, aluminum composite, wood, glass, foam board, and a range of other rigid materials. If you’re not sure what’s best for your application, we’re happy to make a recommendation.

Printing

Your file is printed directly onto the material using UV-cured ink. Our flatbed printer lays down color, white, and specialty ink layers as needed, with the UV curing process happening in real time to produce a sharp, durable, immediately dry finish.

4

Quality Inspection

Each piece is reviewed for color accuracy, print clarity, registration, and surface quality before it moves to packaging. We verify that the finished product matches your file and meets our internal quality standards.

5

Packaging & Delivery

Your completed order is carefully packed and shipped according to your specifications — whether that’s a single custom panel or a bulk run of branded components.

settings.title: Frequently Asked Questions About UV Flatbed Printing

settings.html:
What materials can be UV flatbed printed?

UV flatbed printing is compatible with a wide range of rigid and semi-rigid substrates, including acrylic, polycarbonate, PVC, aluminum, wood, MDF, glass, ceramic tile, and foam board. Because the printer operates on an open flatbed rather than feeding material through a mechanism, it can accommodate most flat, rigid materials regardless of thickness, up to the machine’s maximum height clearance.

How durable is UV flatbed printing?

UV-cured prints are highly durable. The ink bonds directly to the substrate surface and cures to a hard finish that resists scratches, moisture, UV exposure, and general wear. For most indoor applications, UV flatbed prints have an indefinite service life. Outdoor durability varies by substrate and environment, but UV-cured inks generally outperform adhesive-backed graphics significantly in longevity.

What is the difference between UV flatbed printing and screen printing?

Screen printing applies ink through a mesh stencil and is well-suited for very high-volume, single-substrate runs with limited color variation. UV flatbed printing is a digital process with no screen setup, making it faster and more cost-effective for short-to-mid runs, complex designs, full-color photography, and jobs requiring printing on multiple substrates. UV flatbed printing also produces prints with no peeling risk, as the ink is bonded to the surface rather than sitting on top of it.

Can UV flatbed printing be used on clear or transparent acrylic?

Yes. UV flatbed printers can apply a white ink base layer beneath color inks to ensure vibrant, opaque results on clear or transparent substrates. This makes it ideal for back-lit acrylic panels, display components, and decorative applications where clarity of the base material is part of the design.

What file formats do you accept for UV flatbed printing?

We recommend vector formats such as AI, EPS, or PDF for the sharpest output, particularly for text and line work. High-resolution raster files (300 DPI or higher at print size) are also accepted for photographic and complex artwork. Contact us if you have questions about preparing your file for optimal results.

<script>
(function() {
  'use strict';

  /* Scroll-fade animations */
  var observer = new IntersectionObserver(function(entries) {
    entries.forEach(function(entry) {
      if (entry.isIntersecting) entry.target.classList.add('visible');
    });
  }, { threshold: 0.15, rootMargin: '0px 0px -30px 0px' });

  document.querySelectorAll('.cap-page-fade').forEach(function(el) {
    observer.observe(el);
  });

  /* Process carousel dot navigation */
  var track = document.getElementById('processTrack');
  var dotsContainer = document.getElementById('processDots');
  if (track && dotsContainer) {
    var cards = track.querySelectorAll('.process-card');
    cards.forEach(function(_, i) {
      var dot = document.createElement('span');
      if (i === 0) dot.classList.add('active');
      dot.addEventListener('click', function() {
        cards[i].scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'nearest', inline: 'start' });
      });
      dotsContainer.appendChild(dot);
    });

    var dots = dotsContainer.querySelectorAll('span');
    track.addEventListener('scroll', function() {
      var scrollLeft = track.scrollLeft;
      var cardWidth = cards[0].offsetWidth + 24;
      var activeIndex = Math.round(scrollLeft / cardWidth);
      dots.forEach(function(d, i) {
        d.classList.toggle('active', i === activeIndex);
      });
    });
  }

  /* FAQ accordion */
  document.querySelectorAll('.faq-q').forEach(function(q) {
    q.addEventListener('click', function() {
      var item = q.parentElement;
      var wasOpen = item.classList.contains('open');
      document.querySelectorAll('.faq-item').forEach(function(fi) {
        fi.classList.remove('open');
      });
      if (!wasOpen) item.classList.add('open');
    });
  });
})();
</script>
